families.family: Taiwan / ICPC Asia Taiwan Online Programming Contest (TOPC)

facts.participants: Open entry, all Taiwanese universities (international teams admitted for a 1000 NTD fee; domestic free); one coach + 3 contestants + 1 reserve. Runs annually since 2015 (NTU e-paper: 'since 2015 an online contest (TOPC) has been held before the regional'). 2020s editions documented on topc.icpc.tw (2020-2026).
facts.problemset: Own new problemset each year, >=7 English problems, 3h, at least 1/3 solvable in Python 3 (e.g. 2023-TOPC.pdf published on its own site). Not shared with any sibling.
facts.qualification: THE official online preliminary for the Taiwan-hosted ICPC Asia regional (Taipei 2018 @NTU, Taipei-Hsinchu 2020-21, Taoyuan 2023, Taichung 2024-25). Official four-tier domestic priority for the regional: Tier 1 = best team per school (2 for host) ordered by TOPC rank, capped at 30 teams; Tier 2 = top 40 of NCPC (MOE national contest) finals; Tier 3 = up to 10 CPE-recommended teams; Tier 4 = rest by TOPC rank. Priority scheme suspended in any year the lists cannot be fixed 34 days before the regional.
facts.format: ONLINE always (it is in the name); never onsite. 3 hours.
facts.host: Taiwan Association of Programming Contests and Certification (contest manager at NYCU, mzshieh@nycu.edu.tw); regional itself hosted by rotating universities (NTU 2018, NTUB/Taoyuan 2023...).

for: R3 pass: explicitly gates seats/priority at the Taiwan Asia regional (Tier 1 of the official priority list)
R2 pass: unique new problems each year
R1 pass: nationwide multi-university (plus foreign entrants)
against: R4 fail: online every year by design, no COVID excuse
Identity lens: same geography as the parent regional (Taiwan), exists only to seed it, run by the same ICPC-Taiwan apparatus (icpc.tw domain family)
evidence: https://topc.icpc.tw/ (format, eligibility, four-tier priority text, organizer)
https://www.cc.ntu.edu.tw/chinese/epaper/0047/20181220_4703.html (TOPC since 2015 as pre-regional online round; 2018 Asia Taipei regional at NTU; Taiwan hosted 1997/2004/2010/2013/2014 previously)
https://hackmd.io/@jakao/collegiateCompetitionsProgramming (TOPC top ~40 to Taiwan regional; unrestricted entry)
https://topc2023.icpc.tw/2023-TOPC.pdf (own problemset)

families.family: Taiwan / NCPC = MOE National Collegiate Programming Contest (covers the 'Kaohsiung Group-A/B/C 2012' rows; 'Chia-Yi' rows probably earlier editions)

facts.participants: All Taiwanese universities; Group A (甲組) open to all majors, Group B (乙組) restricted to non-CS majors, Group C (丙組) open-source application track. Two simultaneous onsite sites: north = NTNU (Taipei), south = NSYSU (Kaohsiung) — hence CMS rows located 'Kaohsiung' with Group-A/B/C in 2012.
facts.problemset: Own MOE problemsets per year; Groups A/B 5h, Group C 4h. Not shared with TOPC/regional.
facts.qualification: 2012 rules: up to 15 best Group A+B teams recommended to the 'ACM ICPC Asia Taiwan regional' with MOE travel subsidies (up to NT$300k for top 2). Current rules: NCPC finals top 40 = Tier 2 of the official priority list for the Taiwan Asia regional. So it has continuously fed the regional.
facts.format: ONSITE (single-day, two parallel physical sites), no online round in 2012 rules; later years added a preliminary (初賽) + final per community docs.
facts.host: Organizer: Taiwan Ministry of Education (教育部); host sites NTNU + NSYSU (rotating lead: NSYSU 2025 '114年度', NTNU 2026 '115年度'). Government contest, not ICPC-branded, but registered in ICPC CMS.

for: R1/R2/R3/R4 all pass: nationwide multi-university, own problems, onsite, and it gates recommendations + Tier-2 priority into the Taiwan Asia regional
Long continuous history (annual MOE event), independent identity distinct from the ICPC regional
against: It is a Ministry-of-Education championship first; ICPC gating is a side function (recommendation/priority, not the sole path)
Groups B (non-CS majors) and C (open-source) are sector/track-restricted side divisions with no ICPC relevance

'Chia-Yi' rows unverified: most plausibly NCPC editions hosted in Chia-Yi (National Chung Cheng University area) in early years (CMS 2007+), but no online confirmation found — needs-info on those specific rows

families.family: Taiwan / sector contests: TUPC (Technology Universities) & PUPC/NCPU (Private Universities)

facts.participants: Sector-restricted by charter: TUPC = 技專校院 (technological/vocational universities) only, CMS name 'Taiwan National Contest for Technology Universities' 2016-2021, continuing as 'ICPC Taiwan Technology University Programming Contest' (finder editions 2023, 2024, 2026). PUPC/NCPU = private universities/colleges only (全國私立大專校院程式競賽), 15th edition 2025, so running since ~2011; CMS 2021 row = 'The 2021 ICPC-Taiwan National Contest for Private Universities' (slug ICPC-TAIPEI-NCPU-2022).
facts.problemset: Own problemsets per event (ICPC-style, teams of 3, ICPC eligibility rules applied).
facts.qualification: NO place in the current official four-tier priority for the Taiwan Asia regional (that list = TOPC / NCPC / CPE only). A community source (HackMD) records that the technology-university and private-university contests each historically supplied ~10 priority teams to the Taiwan regional, so at most an intermittent, minor feeder role; winners get 'ICPC official certificates' and cash, nothing on the WF path today. R3 essentially fails.
facts.format: ONSITE, single-site, annual; PUPC rotates among private hosts (YZU 2024, Providence University Taichung 2025); TUPC hosted in Taipei in the CMS 2016-2021 years (CMS attributes 'NCTU').
facts.host: PUPC: rotating private university + Taiwan Association of Computer Programming Contest (TCPC) as co-organizer; TUPC: technology-university host (CMS-era Taipei), same ICPC-Taiwan orbit.

for: Independent identity, own problems, onsite — real contests, properly documented
ICPC-registered with ICPC certificates and eligibility rules
against: R1-flavored restriction: closed to a sector subset of universities (not a general national round)
R3 fail (current): no documented gate onto the WF path; regional priority today runs only through TOPC/NCPC/CPE; the historical ~10-slot claim is community-sourced only
evidence: https://sites.google.com/gm.pu.edu.tw/pupc2025/競賽資訊 (private-only eligibility, 15th edition, Providence U host, TCPC co-org, ICPC certificates/eligibility rules)
https://topc.icpc.tw/ (current priority tiers exclude TUPC/PUPC)

families.family: Thailand National On-site Programming Contest + Northern/Northeastern/Southern/Central group rounds

facts.participants: Nationwide. Universities compete first in 4 sector-geographic group rounds — North (Chiang Mai U CS dept, 'first regional round' branding revived 2026), South (PSU/Songkhla Rajabhat 2016), Northeast, Central — then the best advance to the Thailand National round. 2024 national: free registration, teams of 3, at Chulalongkorn.
facts.problemset: Each round has its own problemset (different hosts/dates); no evidence of problem sharing across the four group rounds (unverified — document per R2 if rows are merged).
facts.qualification: Chain confirmed: group rounds -> National round -> international/Asia level. SKRU 2016: 'competitions are organized by universities representing the regions: North, South, Northeast, Central' and winners 'advance to the national level and subsequently to international competition'. CMU 2026: regional round exists 'to select top teams to advance to the national level'. National top teams have historically been funded (SIPA/DEPA & sponsors) into ICPC Asia regionals — Thailand itself hosts them periodically (Phuket 2009/2011, Bangkok 2014, 2016, Nakhon Pathom 2018, Bangkok 2025 @ Chula, onsite 1-2 Nov 2025); PSU Phuket hosted the 2016 World Finals.
facts.format: National round is ONSITE by name and in practice ('Thailand National On-site Programming Contest'; 2024: 'Onsite event for every team', Faculty of Engineering, Chulalongkorn, 7-8 Sep 2024). Group rounds are onsite at the regional host universities.
facts.host: Rotating Thai universities per round (Chula ran both the 2024 National and the 2025 Asia Bangkok regional); national coordination with government software agency (SIPA/DEPA) and ICPC Thailand.

for: National round: R1 pass (nationwide), R3 pass (feeds Thai representation at Asia regionals incl. home Bangkok regional), R4 pass (onsite, explicitly named on-site)
Group rounds have no identity beyond their compass-point geography -> identity lens folds them into the national event as its qualifying stages
against: The precise seat mechanics (how many national teams get Asia regional slots) not found in writing — advancement wording is 'advance to national then international' plus funding, not a published slot table
Group-round problemset independence unverified

families.family: Japan Online First-Round (国内予選, ICPC Japan domestic qualifier)

facts.participants: All Japanese universities; grew 28 teams (1998) to ~300+ (2023); median ~355 in CMS (2017-2027 rows, but the round itself has run every year since 1998 — CMS start is registration lag, not first edition).
facts.problemset: Own problemset every year (domestic set, distinct from the Asia regional set; archives with judge data on icpc.jp since 2003).
facts.qualification: Gates the Asia regional held in Japan: Yokohama 2018-2025 (earlier Tsukuba 2015-17, Aizu 2008/2013, Tokyo, Hakodate, Kanazawa, Kyoto, Fukuoka, Ehime...). 2025 selection rule set by the Japanese ICPC Board: ~49 teams via tiered per-university caps (top 10 all; ranks 11-25 max 3/univ; 26-40 max 2; 41-49 max 1; then one-per-new-university fill).

facts.host: ICPC Japanese steering committee (ICPC 運営委員会) / icpc.jp; JAG (Japanese Alumni Group) supports judging and archives.

families.family: Vietnam National Programming Contest (ICPC Vietnam vòng Quốc gia)

facts.participants: Nationwide, all Vietnamese universities (plus a high-school division in recent years); CMS median ~262 teams (2014-2025); 2024 national drew 713 teams / 2,139 contestants including non-ICPC divisions. Upstream feeders: North/Central/South rounds (vòng Khu vực Bắc-Trung-Nam) each October at centralized onsite sites (2026 hosts: HUST Hanoi, HCMUS HCMC, Hue University of Science); 824 teams at the 2025 Southern round alone.
facts.problemset: Own problemset per round; National round run on an online judge (Kattis 2018-2019 with public mirrors, VNOJ 2024). Regional (Bắc/Trung/Nam) rounds have their own sets.
facts.qualification: Gates the ICPC Asia regional hosted in Vietnam: 'only teams solving at least 1 problem in the ICPC National round are considered for selection into the ICPC Asia Vietnam regional'. The Asia regional is the WF-path event, onsite, co-located with the OLP week (rotating city/host: Hanoi 2006 VNU-UET, Danang 2019, Can Tho 2020, Hanoi/FPT 2021, HCMC/HCMUTE 2022, Hue 2023, Hanoi/HaUI 2024 + Asia-Pacific Championship @ VNU-UET 2024, HCMC/HUTECH 2025). National runs ~1 month before (e.g. 3 Nov 2019; 7-8 Nov 2026), NOT co-located with OLP; OLP itself is a separate individual olympiad by the same organizer.
facts.format: Distributed/hybrid: online judge with teams at multiple centralized, proctored sites nationwide (2026 wording: national round 'at multiple centralized locations'; regional rounds 'thi tập trung' with fees — 550k VND regional, 1.1M VND national). Not a single onsite venue; not a pure at-home online round either.
facts.host: VAIP (Vietnam Association for Information Processing, office@vaip.vn) with rotating host universities; same body runs OLP and the Asia Vietnam regional.

for: R3 pass: explicit written gate into the Asia Vietnam regional (>=1 solved problem requirement + selection)
R1 pass: nationwide, hundreds of teams, dozens of universities
R2 pass: own problems each year
Has its own identity: national championship titles awarded; structured pyramid (regional rounds -> national) beneath it
against: R4 borderline: delivered on an online judge across distributed proctored sites (Kattis/VNOJ), not a single onsite hall — under a strict 'not online' reading it flips to part-of-parent/registry; under 'proctored multi-site = onsite-equivalent' it stays mainline
Same organizer and geography as the parent Asia Vietnam regional (VAIP), which pulls toward part-of-parent

families.family: asia-nationals-misc (Mongolia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Malaysia, Pakistan, Philippines, Afghanistan, D.P.R. Korea)

facts.participants: Per country: MONGOLIA - National Student Programming Olympiad, ~15 teams from 9 universities (2016, 8th ICPC-era edition; olympiad lineage claimed to 1976). MYANMAR - MCPC, national, UCSY + other computer universities (UCSM, MIIT...). BANGLADESH - NCPC, 149 teams from universities across the country (2018). MALAYSIA - al-Khawarizmi National, 13 universities (2018: UTAR, UM, IIUM, Taylor's...). PAKISTAN - national event at FAST-NUCES Lahore, Nov 2014 ('first time in Pakistan'). PHILIPPINES - Philippines National Programming Contest, multi-university (19 PH teams/multiple unis visible at the 2015 Singapore online prelim); some editions in Davao. AFGHANISTAN - national round with only ~3-6 Kabul universities (Kabul U, Kateb U, Polytechnic U; 2017 Kabul regional: 10 teams from 6 universities) - R1 borderline. DPRK - domestic selection among KISU/Kim Chaek UT etc., details unreachable (.kp blocked).
facts.problemset: Each national sets its own problems (no sibling sharing observed).
facts.qualification: MONGOLIA: top 2 teams advance to the Asia regional (explicit, 2016) - R3 PASS. MYANMAR: 'winner teams of MCPC are eligible to participate in the Asia-Yangon Regional' (UCSY-hosted, 2016-2019) - R3 PASS while Yangon existed; both died together after 2019. AFGHANISTAN: national (Sep) precedes and feeds the Asia Kabul Regional (Nov, Kateb-hosted 2017-2019; plus a 2019 Kabul First Round Online) - R3 pass, R1 weak. BANGLADESH: standalone national championship (ICT Division + BCC + rotating host); NO gate into the Dhaka Regional, which runs its own open online preliminary - R3 FAIL. PAKISTAN 2014: nothing downstream existed yet in-country (Lahore online round + finals only from 2016 at UMT; Topi/GIKI regional with 141-team online prelim -> 47 onsite from 2019/2021) - R3 FAIL for the 2014 row. PHILIPPINES: 'Philippines National Round 2014' cited by the Singapore RCD as a recognized feeder; Manila Regional (Ateneo, 2017-2019, 2022) was the domestic WF path it fed - partial R3, mechanics undocumented. DPRK: presumably selected teams for Asia regionals incl. the ACM-ICPC Asia Pyongyang Regional (ran 2015 and 2016 seasons; KISU announced 'the 41th ACM-ICPC Asia Pyongyang Regional'; KISU 'RNS' reached WF2016 Phuket) - year of the CMS national row unresolved.
facts.format: All ONSITE where documented: Ulaanbaatar/NUM (Apr 2016); UCSY Yangon single-stage (Aug 2018); IUBAT Dhaka (Aug 2018, single onsite day); IIUM Kuala Lumpur (May 2018, 5h, 10 problems); FAST-NUCES Lahore (Nov 2014); Kabul Polytechnic gymnasium (Sep 2019); Philippines editions onsite (incl. Davao). DPRK unknown (presumed onsite Pyongyang).

BANGLADESH: rotating university (IUBAT 2018; also JU/Daffodil-era editions) + ICT Division + Bangladesh Computer Council. PHILIPPINES: CSP-orbit rotating hosts; Ateneo de Manila ran the Manila Regional. AFGHANISTAN: Kateb University ('the only representative in Afghanistan based on its agreement with ACM'). DPRK: Kim Il Sung University.

families.family: China provincial/metropolitan opens (Shanghai Metropolitan 2015, Inner Mongolia 2013/14, Dalian Metropolitan 2013, Shandong Province 2022, Shaanxi National 2026)

facts.participants: Open multi-university fields, typically province/metro-wide with invited outside teams; the modern 全国邀请赛 (national invitationals) draw universities nationwide.
facts.problemset: Each event sets its own problems (invitationals/provincials have independent juries).
facts.qualification: Two eras. MODERN (relevant to Shaanxi National 2026, Shandong 2022): ICPC Asia (Beijing HQ, icpc.pku.edu.cn) formally approves 省赛 (2025: Guizhou, Shaanxi/Xidian, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Zhejiang, Xinjiang) and 全国邀请赛 (2025: Wuhan/HUST Apr, Xi'an/NWPU May, Nanchang May, Yinchuan Jun). The 50th Xi'an regional (Oct 2025) slot allocation: 230 slots by online-preliminary school rank (ranks 1-80: 2 slots, 81-150: 1), 120 slots = top-120 schools of the May Shaanxi National Invitational (1 each), 46 contribution slots, plus committee-recommended slots for provincial-contest winners and regional-balance discretion, with per-school caps (WF alumni schools <=4, others <=3). So the National Invitational IS one of the parallel official gates into a regional; provincial contests gate only via discretionary recommendation. HISTORIC rows (Shanghai Metropolitan 2015, Inner Mongolia 2013/14, Dalian Metropolitan 2013): that era's Chinese regionals used open registration/per-school balancing with no provincial gating - independent opens, R3 fail.
facts.format: ONSITE events (provincials/invitationals are weekend onsite contests at the host university; the gate that IS online in China is the separate 网络预选赛 online preliminary, not these).
facts.host: Host universities under ICPC Asia (China) HQ at PKU: e.g. Xidian (Shaanxi provincial), NWPU Xi'an (Silk Road / Shaanxi National Invitational), Shandong hosts for the 2022 provincial; 2013-15 metros by local universities (Shanghai league; Inner Mongolia U; Dalian).

for: Shaanxi 'National Invitational' line: explicit 120-slot table into the Xi'an regional (partial R3 pass) - if any China row graduates from registry, it is this one
All onsite (R4 pass), own problems (R2 pass), multi-university (R1 pass)
against: Shanghai Metropolitan 2015 / Inner Mongolia 2013-14 / Dalian 2013: no qualification function at all in that era - independent opens (R3 fail) -> registry
Provincial contests (incl. Shandong 2022): only discretionary 'committee recommendation' slots, not a published gate - R3 weak
Even the invitational gate is one of five parallel pathways (online preliminary dominates with 230 slots) - these events do not sit ON the WF path so much as beside it
evidence: https://icpc.pku.edu.cn/docs/2025-09/63d703576fef48b3840a1685777a2de1.pdf (50th Xi'an regional slot allocation: 230 online-prelim / 120 Shaanxi National Invitational / 46 contribution / provincial recommendations / caps)
https://icpc.pku.edu.cn/tzgg/1119_icpcbjzb_164509.htm (2025 approved provincial contests and national invitationals with hosts/dates)

families.family: Kharagpur 'North India Area' Programming Contest (2012, 467 teams)

facts.participants: 467 teams, India-wide entry (the 'North India Area' label reflects ICPC-India's 2012 split of coverage between the new Kharagpur site and Amritapuri, not a residency restriction).
facts.problemset: Own online-round problemset (hosted on CodeChef: contest code ACMKGP13, 'ACM-ICPC Asia-Kharagpur Site First Round Online').
facts.qualification: It was the online First Round gating the onsite ACM-ICPC Asia Kharagpur Regional at IIT Kharagpur - IIT KGP's first year as an Asia regional site (onsite Dec 2012, WF2013 season; the site then ran annually with a CodeChef online round through the late 2010s). So it gated a real WF-path regional that ran AFTER it - R3 pass in the correct direction.
facts.format: ONLINE (CodeChef-hosted), one-off under the 'North India Area' name; subsequent years were branded 'Kharagpur Site Online/First Round'.
facts.host: IIT Kharagpur (regional host) with CodeChef as the online platform.

notes: R4 FLIP LIST - families whose proposal flips if 'mainline = not online' were relaxed: Taiwan TOPC, Korea National First Round, Japan Online First-Round, Indonesia INC, and Kharagpur North India Area 2012 are all pure-online rounds that otherwise pass R1/R2/R3 with large fields; under a permissive R4 each would be a mainline national/area preliminary, under strict R4 they are part-of-parent regardless of size. Vietnam National is the borderline case: online judge (Kattis/VNOJ) but proctored multi-site 'thi tập trung' delivery - it flips between mainline and part-of-parent depending on how R4 treats proctored distributed rounds. Everything else evaluated here (Thailand national, Taiwan NCPC, all misc nationals, China provincials/invitationals) is onsite where documented, so R4 does not move them.

Direction-of-gating check (R3 'beware events running AFTER what they'd feed'): all confirmed gates here run BEFORE their parent (TOPC Sep -> regional Nov; Korea prelim Oct -> Seoul Nov; Japan Jul -> Yokohama Nov-Dec; INC Oct -> Jakarta Nov-Dec; Vietnam national Nov -> Asia Dec; Thailand groups -> national Sep -> Bangkok Nov; MCPC Aug -> Yangon regional autumn; Afghanistan national Sep -> Kabul regional Nov; Mongolia national Apr -> Asia regional autumn; Shaanxi invitational May -> Xi'an regional Oct). No after-the-fact gating claims were found.

Problemset sharing (R2 documentation): no problemset sharing across siblings was found anywhere in these families - Thailand's four group rounds and Vietnam's three Khu vực rounds are run by different hosts on different dates and appear to set independent problems, but this is inferred, not verified; if those rows are merged into their national parents, mark problem-sharing status 'unverified' rather than 'unique'.

Taiwan row accounting: the 39 CMS rows most plausibly decompose into TOPC annuals (2015+), MOE-NCPC site/group rows (Kaohsiung Group-A/B/C 2012 = NCPC south site at NSYSU with its three statutory groups; north site NTNU the same day), TUPC 2016-2021(+2023-2026) and PUPC/NCPU rows. The 'Chia-Yi' rows remain the one unresolved identity - hypothesis: NCPC editions hosted in Chia-Yi (National Chung Cheng University), consistent with the 2007+ date range, but unconfirmed (needs-info).

Taiwan regional context for the archive: Taiwan-hosted Asia regionals per NTU e-paper: 1997, 2004, 2010, 2013, 2014, then annually-ish 2015?-2018 (NTU 2018), 2020-21 Taipei-Hsinchu, Taoyuan 2023, Taichung 2024-25 - the TOPC rows should attach to whichever of these is the archive's parent series.

Tooling caveats hit during research: icpc.global finder pages are JS-only and its JSON API guesses 404 - CMS row names were cross-checked via search-result titles only; zh.wikipedia is cache-only (unfetchable); .kp (Kim Il Sung University) unreachable; ncpc.mist.ac.bd is domain-squatted with gambling spam (dead-link hazard if the archive cites it); codeforces.com and codechef.com refuse fetches (403/robots); penoy.admu.edu.ph (Manila regional archive) DNS-dead.
